title: Monitoring minimization, private communication, and emotion-recognition refusal

observations.claim: ICO guidance treats monitoring that may lead to performance management, financial loss, keystroke capture or profiling as potentially high risk and supports pre-deployment DPIA and worker consultation.
ICO guidance requires purpose clarity, accuracy, correction and a worker opportunity to explain or challenge monitoring results.
Meaningful human review requires active checking, competence and authority to go against a system recommendation rather than routine application.
The Platform Work Directive prohibits processing private conversations, off-work data, predictions of fundamental-rights exercise and inferences about trade-union membership, disability or health.
limits: Platform-work scope and transposition boundary remain explicit.

observations.claim: The EU AI Act prohibition on workplace emotion recognition has applied since 2025-02-02, subject to its stated exceptions.
limits: Medical and safety exceptions and exact system classification remain open.

observations.claim: EU high-risk employment AI obligations remain on a later application timeline, recorded here as 2027-12-02 rather than treated as operative on 2026-08-01.
limits: Current implementation timeline only; no premature promotion.

findings.claim: Some data should never become a management signal: private representative communications, off-duty behavior and predictions of rights exercise are counterpower boundaries, not missing features.
Emotion inference is not pastoral care; converting voice, face or behavior into an emotional-risk score can move welfare language into control.
limits: No named vendor misuse or universal outcome claim.

findings.claim: Monitoring accuracy is inseparable from due process when the output enters appraisal, restriction or discipline.
limits: UK guidance and transaction-specific legal application.

findings.claim: Future high-risk duties cannot be used as evidence of present compliance, while current prohibitions must not be deferred merely because other AI Act duties are pre-effective.
